sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in React and its state tool, the task and status types, the single card component and the shared store. Marks the file as running in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the board needs browser events for drag and drop, and needs the store to change status.
sections.watch_out: Moving cards depends on the store's status action, so if that action breaks, both drag and drop stop working.

sections.name: TaskKanbanProps
sections.title: Inputs for the board
sections.what: Says the board takes one input, the list of tasks to show.
sections.why: Likely reason: the parent screen decides which tasks match its filters, so the board only arranges what it receives.
sections.watch_out: The board does no filtering itself, so it shows exactly the list it is handed.

sections.name: TaskKanban (part 1)
sections.title: Column setup, drag handlers and phone list
sections.what: Defines the six status columns with their titles and colors. Sets up handlers for dragging over a column and dropping a card. On small screens, shows every task in one list with a message when the list is empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: the column setup is kept in one place so the board and its drop targets always match. Drag data is stored under two names, likely for compatibility with differing browser behavior.
sections.watch_out: The drop handler reads two possible data names, so renaming one of them in the drag start handler can break dropping without an error.

sections.name: TaskKanban (part 2)
sections.title: Desktop status columns
sections.what: On medium and larger screens, draws six columns side by side. Each column shows its title, a count of its tasks, and its cards. Cards can be dragged, and dropping one on a column changes its status to that column's status.
sections.why: Likely reason: a board gives a quick view of progress and lets the user change status by moving cards.
sections.watch_out: Each card is drawn in both the phone list and the desktop board, so every task exists twice in the page even though only one copy is visible.

summary: Shows tasks as a six-column status board on larger screens, and as one plain list on phones, with drag and drop to change status.
purpose: Let the user see work grouped by status and move a card to a new status by dragging it.
why: Likely reason: a six-column board does not fit a phone screen, so small screens get a single list instead.
how: 1. Receives the already filtered task list from its parent. 2. On small screens, draws every task as one list. 3. On medium and larger screens, sorts tasks into six columns by status and draws each column with a count. 4. When a card is dragged and dropped on a column, the store changes that task to the column's status.
inputs: A list of tasks from the parent screen. Drag data comes from the browser drag events.
outputs: Visual columns and lists. A dropped card updates the task status through the store.
risks: Every task is drawn twice, once in the list and once in the board, and the hidden copy still exists in the page. A mobile status value is declared but not used in the shown code.
debug: If a card will not move, check that the drop handler receives a task id and that toggleTaskStatus works. If a card shows in the wrong column, check its status value. If the page feels slow with many tasks, check how many copies of each card are drawn.
